title: Specified strict-perfect models under arbitrary ringed-topos derived pullback
statement: Let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $R,S$ sheaves of commutative rings and coefficient map $u^{-1}R\to S$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and ordinary module pullback $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ and its K-flat derived functor with comparison $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of $R$-module sheaves with a specified strict-perfect package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]: $F^r=0$ outside $[a,b]\subset\mathbf Z$, and maps $i_r:F^r\to R^{\oplus N_r}$, $p_r:R^{\oplus N_r}\to F^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Then every term of $F^\bullet$ is flat and $F^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The termwise complex $u^*F^\bullet$ is zero outside the same interval. Under the canonical finite-free identification $\gamma_r:u^*(R^{\oplus N_r})\cong S^{\oplus N_r}$ its maps $i^u_r=\gamma_r u^*i_r$ and $p^u_r=u^*p_r\gamma_r^{-1}$ satisfy $p^u_ri^u_r=1$, so it has a specified strict-perfect package with the same ranks. It too is K-flat with flat terms. The canonical comparison $\epsilon_F:Lu^*(Q_RF^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(u^*F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. For any derived isomorphism $e:Q_RF^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, the isomorphism $\epsilon_F\circ Lu^*(e^{-1})$ identifies $Lu^*P$ with this specified termwise strict-perfect model. For every chain map $v:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ between such bounded packaged complexes, $Q_S(u^*v)\circ\epsilon_F=\epsilon_G\circ Lu^*(Q_Rv)$. No flatness of the coefficient map, global projectivity of the sheaf objects, or exactness of $u^*$ on all modules is assumed.

proof.text: Fix a degree $r$ and put $M=F^r$, $N=N_r$. The tensor definition gives $H\otimes_R R^{\oplus N}\cong H^{\oplus N}$: send $h\otimes(r_j)_j$ to $(r_jh)_j$, with inverse $(h_j)_j\mapsto\sum_jh_j\otimes e_j$. These maps commute with restriction and hence induce inverse maps on sheafifications. Tensoring $i_r,p_r$ makes the sequence obtained by tensoring any short exact sequence with $M$ a retract of its $N$-fold direct sum. Here exactness of the finite sum is checked coordinatewise, using a common refinement of the finitely many local lifts for the surjection. Exactness passes to this retract directly: a section in a kernel is included into the larger kernel, locally lifted there, and projected back; injectivity and surjectivity follow by the same inclusion and projection. Thus $-\otimes_R M$ is exact, so $M$ is flat. This argument is valid for any commutative ring sheaf and any finite-free splitting; it also covers $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 03EU, lemma-colimits-flat, finite sums; elementary finite-free coordinate calculation and retract argument

proof.text: The specified bound gives $F^r=0$ for $r>b$, and step 1 gives flatness in every degree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] with upper bound $b$ on the given small site. Its tensor is exactly the sheafified sectionwise tensor used here. Hence $F^\bullet$ is K-flat. No categorical projectivity of its terms is needed.

Write $A=u^{-1}R$. Since the inverse image of a morphism of topoi preserves finite products, its transported module structure identifies $u^{-1}(R^{\oplus N})$ with $A^{\oplus N}$, with the standard coordinate maps. After this identification define $\gamma:S\otimes_A A^{\oplus N}\to S^{\oplus N}$ by $s\otimes(a_j)_j\mapsto(s c(a_j))_j$. Its inverse sends $(s_j)_j$ to $\sum_j s_j\otimes e_j$; the balanced relation checks both composites are identities. These are maps of sheaves by the tensor definition. The same formula shows $u^*0=0$. Pullback is a functor, so its images of the differentials still have consecutive composite zero. Thus the termwise pullback is a complex, zero outside $[a,b]$. For each $r$, conjugating the pulled splitting by $\gamma_r$ gives $p^u_ri^u_r=u^*p_r\gamma_r^{-1}\gamma_ru^*i_r=u^*(p_ri_r)=1$. These are the required specified splittings of the same ranks, with no assertion that the splittings are chain maps.

source.place: Tag 08H3, lemma-strictly-perfect-pullback; explicit finite-free identification from sites-modules.tex Tag 03DF, lemma-global-pullback

proof.text: Apply the coordinate and retract argument of step 1 over $S$ to the splittings just constructed. Every term of $u^*F^\bullet$ is flat. This complex is bounded above by $b$, so [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] on the target site makes it K-flat as well. This uses neither flatness of $A\to S$ nor exactness of $u^*$ on arbitrary modules.

The source complex is K-flat with flat terms by steps 1 and 2, so the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] gives the isomorphism $\epsilon_F:Lu^*(Q_RF^\bullet)\to Q_S(u^*F^\bullet)$. For a derived isomorphism $e:Q_RF^\bullet\to P$, functoriality shows $Lu^*(e^{-1})$ is inverse to $Lu^*(e)$, so composing it with $\epsilon_F$ gives the claimed isomorphism from $Lu^*P$. Finally pass a chain map $v:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ to the homotopy category and evaluate the naturality square of the same canonical transformation $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$. It reads exactly $Q_S(u^*v)\circ\epsilon_F=\epsilon_G\circ Lu^*(Q_Rv)$. No choice of inverse comparison or resolution is substituted for this transformation.
